products: DesktopLanguageLifecycle (packages/vue-vscode/src/desktopLanguageLifecycle.ts): one activation epoch per started client (the initial start and every restart). Exit, connection-failure, failed-start and silent-server reports carry their epoch; the current epoch enters recovery exactly once and a replaced client's reports (including its type-provider status) are stale

Bounded crash-recovery policy and failure UX: the restart supervisor (packages/vue-vscode/src/restart.ts) is the single recovery authority. The language client's own restart-on-close is disabled through an errorHandler that reports the loss and returns DoNotRestart; three connection errors are tolerated and the fourth shuts the connection down and recovers it. A start that fails enters the same bounded recovery. The type-provider status bar item shows `restarting (n/max)` during recovery and `stopped` (click restarts) after the give-up or a failed manual restart (computeLifecycleStatusBarState in packages/vue-vscode/src/statusBar.ts)

Subscription/process disposal tests: packages/vue-vscode/src/extensionStartAttemptLifetime.spec.ts (start attempt, recovery and activation-on-demand cases), packages/vue-vscode/src/desktopLanguageLifecycle.spec.ts, and the real extension-host suite packages/vue-vscode/e2e/suite/server-lifecycle.test.ts (OS process table under the extension host plus the diagnostics VS Code holds)
retiredRoutes: The language client's DefaultErrorHandler restart-on-close, which restarted the server behind the supervisor and forgot crashes older than three minutes, so a server that kept dying slowly was restarted forever
Failing the start attempt on a failed initial client.start(): the attempt and its status were discarded and the next opened framework document started a fresh attempt with a fresh retry budget

The second verter.typeProvider configuration listener in activateExtension, which restarted a running server a second time beside the debounced restart-required listener, and started a server nobody asked for when none was running
The context.subscriptions fallback in activateVueLanguageServer (a start attempt without an owning lifetime); the activation-owned lifetime is now a required option
migration: No setting, command, activation event or protocol message changes. A failed manual restart now leaves the server visibly stopped instead of silently stopped. Changing verter.typeProvider restarts a running server once (through the restart-required settings listener) and no longer starts one when none is running; the next framework document starts it.
preservedOwners: activation gate and activation session (activationGate.ts, activationSession.ts)
heartbeat watchdog (now reporting the epoch lost instead of calling the supervisor directly)
shared editor engines: only server-announced owned type-provider pids are ever killed; the shared tsgo tier is never announced
semantic algorithms, project resolution, TypeScript projection and edit transactions (untouched)

cases.binding: e2e/suite/server-lifecycle.test.ts `restart loops replace the one server and never duplicate diagnostics` (three restarts in the real host: exactly one verter-lsp under the extension host, each replaced pid gone, the unsaved edit's diagnostic count unchanged) and `a crashed server is replaced once by the bounded recovery and keeps the unsaved edit`; src/extensionStartAttemptLifetime.spec.ts `restarts a running server exactly once when the type provider changes`, `restarts a crashed server through the supervisor once, never through the client`, and the existing ownership/disposal cases

src/extensionStartAttemptLifetime.spec.ts `recovers a server that cannot start within the budget, then shows it stopped and releases everything on disposal` and `ends a crash loop in a visible stopped state that only a manual restart leaves` (1 + maxAutomaticRestarts starts, one status bar item in the stopped state, quiescent timers); src/restart.spec.ts supervisor cap/backoff/health-window cases

deterministic cells only: activation awaits no server start and spawns none without a framework document (`starts no server without a framework document, even when a server setting changes`); concurrent demand shares one start (existing `language server ownership through runtime publication` cases); the eleven activation events are unchanged (no workspaceContains scan). The startup-latency cell is row VSC1-resource-startup-latency of evidence run vsc8-vscode-desktop-canaries on bench-m3 (VSC8)

the restart supervisor is the one recovery authority and DesktopLanguageLifecycle the one epoch/state owner; errorHandler.closed returns DoNotRestart (asserted by `restarts a crashed server through the supervisor once, never through the client`, and in the real host by the crash case's absence of the client's `Server will restart` line). Retired routes are listed above

no cache, mapping, snapshot, result-handle or incremental-publication change. The only basis rule touched is stale rejection of a replaced client's reports: `never shows a replaced client's engine status as the current one` and the desktopLanguageLifecycle.spec.ts epoch cases

deterministic cells: server process count (one verter-lsp under the extension host), client start counts per crash/restart, and zero armed timers after give-up or disposal are asserted. Rows predeclared for VSC8's vsc8-vscode-desktop-canaries run on bench-m3: VSC1-resource-startup-latency (activation to first ready), VSC1-resource-restart-latency (restart command to replacement ready), VSC1-resource-crash-recovery-latency (process exit to replacement ready), VSC1-resource-retained-memory (extension host RSS after ten restarts versus after the first start). Those timing and memory cells are unavailable on the landing worker and are not reported as numbers

not applicable: no new command, view or protocol operation is introduced; the lifecycle state is shown on the existing type-provider status bar item and runs the existing verter.restartLanguageServer command
